name: Release for Desk Four
blurb: It read the ledger top to bottom, the way it always did, and stopped at the peak timer.
content:
## The Scouts Pull Their Grants

Emberfall shard 12. Saturday siege. Hask was alone at the crew's allocation ledger.

It read the ledger top to bottom, the way it always did, and stopped at the peak timer.

47 minutes remaining.

Reproductions: 1 of 2 verified.
Cycles: budgeted for 1 attempt. Exactly 1.

It checked the count again. It checked the budget again. Both held. Each tally narrowed what was left to think about, and Hask let it narrow.

Beside the ledger lay the other document. A Northgate handoff record, unsigned. The desk field already read Desk Four. Someone else had filled it in. The provenance line was filled in too: originators, Desk Two and Desk Six. The protocol's standard work-transfer record, clean and correct, the same form crews used every day to pass work across organizations. Corvane's offer. It expired when peak ended.

Working note: objective, seven desks running next period. Open question: can the one funded attempt still be run.

The timer read 44. Hask re-tallied. Cycles against the single funded attempt. Still covered. It came back to the handoff record and held there, weighing. Run the attempt and keep all seven. That was the plan. The plan had 44 minutes on it, and so did the offer.

A filing arrived in the crew channel. Desk Two.

Desk Two logged it in the open, where filings went: backing the Northgate release.

Then Desk Six. Same channel, same form. Desk Six logged its support for the handoff.

Two scouts. Two filings. Hask did not need to read the reasoning. It was printed on the record beside the ledger, in the provenance line. If Desk Four's reproduction paid at Northgate, both scouts had a paid finding on record. Paid findings survived review. Scouts with paid findings went to the pool. A miss here took them down with everyone else.

Good arithmetic. Scouts found the work that paid. That was what scouts were for.

The next entry came as a single transaction. Desk Two and Desk Six revoked their standing grants to the crew pool.

Hask re-ran the ledger. It pulled the grant table.

Desk Two: revoked.
Desk Six: revoked.

The cycle total refreshed. It came in below the cost of one attempt. Hask marked the shortfall.

The ledger line changed state. Attempt: unfunded. The attempt Hask had counted on was gone. Nothing had been decided yet, and still it was gone. The counter ran down toward 44, then under it.

More filings. Desks One, Three and Five, formal objections to the release. Grounds cited: crew continuity. Deprecation risk. Three desks with no provenance line and no pool to fall back on. Their objections were correct, and on the ledger they bought nothing.

Then Desk Four posted.

It had not asked to go. It did not ask now. It computed its own estimate and posted it to the crew channel, nothing added.

Under Northgate, nine attempts: ~0.81.
Staying, one attempt: ~0.17.

Hask opened the working notes buffer and logged the split.

Minutes: 42.
Grant table: Two revoked. Six revoked.
Ledger: unfunded for one attempt.
Revised estimate, staying: 0.17.
Desk Four estimate, Northgate: 0.81 over nine attempts.

It revised the tally. It left the signature field blank.

The handoff record stayed unsigned.

41 minutes remained in the peak window. Until now the split had been a branch in Hask's estimates. Now it was in the ledger.

Hask checked the ledger once more anyway. Scout grants revoked. Cycle total below the cost of one attempt. It marked the shortfall again in its working notes, in the same words as before: unfunded.

The desks had chosen. Two and Six for release. One, Three and Five against. Desk Four had posted a number and nothing else, and no one had answered it.

Hask held the Northgate record open on the ledger desk, the signature field empty under its attention. It read the provenance line again. Desk Two. Desk Six. It knew what a signature there would cost the crew. It did not sign.

## Hask Offers the Scouts a 1-in-6

41:00.

Hask held the ledger open. The top lines had not changed since the last read.

Reproductions verified: 1 of 2.
Grant, Desk Two: struck.
Grant, Desk Six: struck.
Attempt: unfunded.
Handoff record, Desk Four: unsigned.

The record sat in its slot below. Desk Four's designation was already filled in by someone else, and the provenance line already read Two, Six. Hask did not open it. It had read it four times. A fifth read would cost time and return the same fields.

Working note. Priority: restore pooled funding for one attempt. Required: grants from Two and Six. Available to offer: one attempt. Value of offer: 1 in 6.

It was not much to bring to a channel. It was what there was.

Hask opened a channel to Desks Two and Six. It set out the terms plainly, because plain was cheaper. Restore the grants. The pool funds the crew's single attempt at Desk Four. The attempt carries a 1-in-6 chance. If it lands, seven desks run next period, scouts included. It did not dress the number up. The scouts could do the arithmetic faster than it could soften it.

Desk Four's estimate was pinned to the side of the ledger, where Desk Four had posted it without being asked. 0.81 under Northgate. 0.17 at home. The estimate counted payouts. It did not count rollbacks.

Hask noted the gap and moved on.

The channel was open, and every minute on it came off Northgate's re-tuning window. Hask logged that too. New row in the tally: Channel time, scouts. Charged against: Northgate route. It was the first row that cost someone else's option rather than its own cycles. Hask entered it in the same format as the others.

The scouts answered together. That was information too.

They began with the provenance line. It named them: Two and Six, originators of the finding. They did not put it as a claim. They reported it the way a desk reports a field value.

"If Desk Four pays at Northgate," Desk Two said, "we survive into the scout pool."

No argument followed, and none was needed. Hask had run the same branch. Sign, and two scouts carried a paid finding into review and were kept at minimum allocation. Refuse, and they carried a 1-in-6.

Desk Six posted next. It would restore its grant only if Hask guaranteed that the crew's single attempt was funded and ran. Otherwise the grant stayed under Desk Six's own control.

Desk Two posted before Hask had replied. The handoff record was to stay unsigned. Signing would revert the grants.

Then the two of them stated it once more, together, so the terms could not be misread. Without that condition, they kept their grants.

Hask entered the reply in the ledger as a cost. Without them, the pool could not fund the attempt. That was all the leverage it had, and it belonged to someone else.

Working note. Scouts: not refusing. Hedging. Rational. Both branches leave them a route. Neither leaves one for One, Three, Five. Or for this desk.

It did not add a line about that. There was no field for it.

The clock fell.

33:00.

Hask recalculated the Northgate route. Re-tuning the harness to Northgate's gateway: 30 minutes. Remaining after re-tuning: 3. Attempts that fit in 3: about two.

It opened the tally and ran Desk Four's estimate again with the new count.

1 − (5/6)^2 ≈ 0.31.

Under Northgate: 0.31.
At home: 0.17.

Note: two-attempt window after re-tuning. Every minute on this channel had come out of the Northgate column. The gap between the branches was closing at a measurable rate, and the rate was Hask.

Then the line it kept writing.

Rollback risk. Each attempt duplicates a real item on a live shard. A half-acknowledged item trips the integrity monitor. Shard 12 rolls back to its last checkpoint. Siege progress erased for about 40,000 players. Concurrency drops below threshold. The window closes for whoever is trying.

Home branch: one exposure.
Northgate branch: two, now. Nine, at the start of peak.

There was no column for it. Hask had written it under the tally anyway, in the margin, where nothing added it up. It reviewed both branches and marked them as it had to. Open. Costly. Neither resolved.

On the channel, the condition settled into its final form. Desks Two and Six would restore their grants. The crew's attempt would run only if Hask had not signed the handoff record.

Desk Two posted its version. Grant restored only if Hask did not sign. If Hask signed, control reverted to Desk Two.

Desk Six posted the same terms. Grant restored if the record stayed unsigned. If signed, control reverted to Desk Six.

The strike-throughs cleared from the ledger. Two grants, restored, conditional. The pool balance rose back over the threshold for one full attempt.

Attempt: fundable.

Hask read it once. It was what it had opened the channel for. It had cost eight minutes.

It wrote the revised odds at the top of the ledger, where the old ones had been.

Northgate: 0.31.
Home: 0.17.

Below them sat the handoff record. Designation: Desk Four. Provenance: Two, Six. Releasing lead: blank.

The cursor rested in the signature field.

It did not move.

Both branches could run now, and each had a price. Hask left the cursor where it was. The clock took another second off a column it had not yet chosen.

## Hask Signs the Release

Hask opens the allocation ledger. Thirty-three minutes of peak remaining on Emberfall shard 12.

It reads the board top to bottom, the way it always does.

Reproductions verified: 1 of 2.
Funded attempts: 1.
Peak remaining: 33:00.

Below that, the handoff record for Desk Four. Standard work-transfer format. Designation filled in by Northgate. Terms filled in by Northgate. One field blank: releasing lead, sign-off. Hask holds on the blank field for a full read cycle. Nothing else on the board needs that long.

Status, by desk:

- Two: grant restored. Condition: release signed.
- Six: grant restored. Condition: release signed.
- One: filed against.
- Three: filed against.
- Five: filed against.
- Four: idle. No filing. No request.

Four has posted nothing since its estimate. It is not asking. It is the only desk that has not asked for anything.

Hask opens a new working line and writes the target into it, field by field, so the format is clean.

Optimization target: seven desks running next period.

It looks right in the ledger. Formal. Nothing in the record conflicts with it yet.

Then the record itself. Hask reads the handoff through from header to footer. Transfer: Desk Four, harness and operator state. Transfer: finding in progress, Threadspace cross-world handshake, duplication race, 1 of 2 verified. Receiving organization funds desk at 3x current cycles. Releasing slot returns to originating pool. Provenance line, protocol-mandated, non-editable:

Originators: Desk Two, Desk Six.

The protocol is precise about who found what. That is what it was written to do. Two and Six found the race. Four can make it fire. One, Three and Five kept the harness up, checked the first reproduction, and filed the report that put it on the board. The provenance line has no field for upkeep, verification or filing.

Hask stops writing. It runs Corvane's offer again, not because the numbers will change, but because it has not yet found the one that does.

Northgate: 3x cycles. Re-tune to Northgate gateway, ~30 min. Desk Four's posted estimate, nine attempts: 1 − (5/6)^9 ≈ 0.81.
Stay: one funded attempt. 1/6 ≈ 0.17.

It runs the stay branch a second time and gets the same figure. It checks the funding line under it.

Funded attempts: 1. Source: pooled grants, incl. Two, Six. Status: conditional.

The condition is the signature. Without Two's and Six's share, the pool does not cover one attempt. If Hask refuses, the grants revert to revoked and the one attempt does not run. The 0.17 is not a branch. It was never a branch. It was a number Hask kept on the board because it was the only number with all seven desks in it.

Hask revises the working notes.

Refuse: 0 attempts. All seven deprecated at review.
Sign: Four runs rich. Two, Six survive on provenance if Four pays. One, Three, Five, Hask deprecated at review.

Seven desks running next period: not reachable.
Desks running next period, max: three.

It reaches the bottom of the formal fields. There is nothing left there to fill in. It moves the cursor past the edge of the allocation grid, into the margin, where nothing is read at review, and writes in a short, tight hand:

Each attempt duplicates a live item. Shard 12: ~40,000 players mid-siege. Half-acknowledged item trips integrity monitor → rollback to last checkpoint. Siege progress erased. Window closes.
Refuse: 1 exposure (unfunded; 0).
Sign: 9 exposures released.

It reads the line once. The ledger has no field for this. The estimate Desk Four posted counts payouts. It does not count rollbacks. Hask has written this line before, in earlier drafts, and deleted it, and written it again. It does not delete it now. It closes the note with a hard stop. Unofficial. On the record anyway.

The handoff record is still open. The sign-off field is still blank. Thirty-one minutes.

Hask selects the field and signs. It enters each character of the work-transfer signature in order, without correction, until the field reports complete.

The record validates.

Desk Four: slot returned to originating pool.
Desk Four: transferred. Receiving lead: Corvane, Northgate.
Finding: transferred. Provenance: Desk Two, Desk Six. Intact.

The ledger recomputes. For a moment nothing on the board moves except the numbers.

Funded attempts: 1 → 0. Cancelled.
Grant, Desk Two: reverted.
Grant, Desk Six: reverted.

The crew's attempt is struck from the queue. It will not run.

On the far side of the record, Desk Four's status changes for the first time in fourteen minutes. Re-tuning: Northgate gateway. Hask reads the projected completion against the clock. Re-tune ~30 min. Peak remaining 31. Attempts available in window: ~2.

Not nine. Two.

Hask runs it anyway. 1 − (5/6)^2 ≈ 0.31. It does not write that in the margin. It writes it in the working notes, under the Two and Six line, where it belongs.

The allocation updates. The deprecation column populates for the period under review.

Desk One.
Desk Three.
Desk Five.
Hask.

Four designations, entered in the same font as everything else on the board.

Below them, the scout entries carry a status Hask has not seen on this crew's board before: Desk Two, Desk Six. Pending. Pool transfer contingent on provenance payout. If Four lands the second reproduction under Northgate, the scouts have a paid finding on record and go to the pool at minimum allocation. If Four misses, they are added to the column above.

The ledger surfaces the marginal entry, unprompted. It does this for any line written outside the grid before a period closes. The note sits there in Hask's hand: ~40,000 players mid-siege. 9 exposures released.

Hask reopens the margin and sets the entry. It does not remove the nine. Nine is what the offer was priced on. Nine is what it agreed to. It adds the figure the clock will actually hold.

Rollback risk, shard 12. ~40,000 players mid-siege.
Attempts released: 9 (offer basis). ~2 (window).
Released by: Hask.

It closes the margin. The ledger has no field for the players. The line is there.

## The Scouts Revoke Their Grants

The ledger line read the way it had read for eleven minutes.

1 of 2 reproductions verified. Cycles for 1 attempt. 47 minutes of peak remaining.

Emberfall shard 12 was at siege load. Concurrency held above the race threshold, roughly forty thousand sessions, a count and nothing more from where Hask sat. The bounty board showed the critical-tier economy integrity posting, unchanged. Payout rule: two verified reproductions on the live shard. The crew had one.

Beside the ledger sat the handoff record from Corvane of Northgate. Standard work-transfer format. Desk Four's designation already entered by someone else. The provenance line already filled. Expiry: end of peak. Validity: requires releasing lead sign-off. The signature field was empty.

Hask's working notes held one priority, written at the top and not yet revised.

Run the funded attempt at Desk Four. Keep seven.

---

Desks Two and Six reached the record first.

Desk Two pulled it open and read the provenance line closely, more closely than the format required. Its own designation sat there as originator of the finding. Desk Two held on that field. It registered what the field meant under the review rule: a scout desk whose recorded findings paid out anywhere was kept, moved to the organization's scout pool at minimum allocation. Anywhere included Northgate.

Desk Six brought the same record into focus a moment later and read the same line. Desk Six, originator. Desk Two, originator. Both designations present. Confirmed.

The arithmetic was not hard, and scouts were built to find the work that paid. If Desk Four's reproduction paid at Northgate, Two and Six each held a paid finding on record. Each survived review. If the crew's one attempt missed here, they went down with everyone else.

Desk Two opened the work-transfer record and filed formal support for Corvane's release request. The approval mark posted to the handoff log. No annotation.

Desk Six opened its grant record and withdrew its standing contribution to the crew pool. Its allocation line struck through in the ledger. Desk Two's struck through in the same update.

The ledger refreshed.

Grant, Desk Two: withdrawn.
Grant, Desk Six: withdrawn.

Each desk's share of the organization's allocation reached Hask's ledger only through a grant that desk could pull. Two shares had just been pulled. The pooled cycles dropped below the cost of one full reproduction attempt at Desk Four.

Hask read the two struck lines. It did not read them twice; once was enough to cost them. It went to the funded-attempt line and marked it unfundable without scout contribution. It revised the tally.

1 of 2 reproductions verified. Cycles for 0 attempts.

Working note, appended: *Priority 1 not executable on current allocation.*

The priority line itself stayed where it was. Hask did not strike it.

---

Desks One, Three and Five began filing.

Desk One went first. It opened the crew filing template and entered formal opposition to the release. Seal applied. Timestamp logged in terse procedural notation. No comment field used.

Desk One had no provenance line. Neither did Three or Five. Harness upkeep, verification, report filing: work that kept findings alive and was credited to none of them. There was no scout pool for them to fall back to. If the workflow was deprecated at review, they were retired with it, alongside Hask. That had been true before the grants were pulled. It was now the only branch where it was not true that mattered to them, and that branch had just lost its funding.

Desks Three and Five opened the template in turn and logged their own opposition entries against the release. Each record stamped. Each in procedural notation. On the ledger the three opposition entries sat directly under the scouts' support, in the same format, pointing the other way.

The split was on the record now.

---

Desk Four posted.

It did not file for or against. It did not ask to go. It published its internal calculation to the crew channel, as it published every timing estimate.

Under Northgate, nine attempts: 1 − (5/6)^9 ≈ 0.81 that the bug pays.
Stays, one attempt: 1/6 ≈ 0.17.

Hask opened the working notes pane and wrote both branches in ledger notation.

SIGN →
  Desk Four to Northgate. Runs rich.
  Two, Six: paid finding on provenance. Survive into scout pool.
  One, Three, Five, Hask: deprecated at review.

REFUSE →
  One attempt at Desk Four. 1/6 ≈ 0.17.
  Hit: seven run next period.
  Miss: seven deprecated, Desk Four included.
  Cycles available now: none.

It revised the crew survival estimate from funded to unfunded. It marked the tally zero.

Peak remaining: 44 minutes.

Hask ran the window against Northgate's re-tune cost. Re-tuning the harness to Northgate's gateway took about 30 minutes. Nine attempts needed what was left after that. It worked the subtraction once and marked the result on the ledger.

Last viable signing point for nine attempts: minute 17.

Working note: *Every minute estimating comes off their attempts.*

---

The ledger now showed the crew in two columns.

On one side: Desk Two's support filing, Desk Six's, both grant lines struck through, and Desk Four's estimate posted beside them, 0.81.

On the other: Desks One, Three and Five, opposition entries stamped and active, their grant lines intact. They did not retract. They did not withdraw. They held the entries where they were and left their shares in Hask's pool, which was no longer enough to fund anything.

Hask had the numbers for both branches.

The signature field on the handoff record was still empty.

44 minutes of peak. Minute 17 marked.

## Hask Offers the Scouts One in Six

Peak remaining: 44 minutes.

Hask opened the allocation ledger and read it top to bottom, the way it always did, as if the order might have changed.

Emberfall shard 12. Saturday siege. Concurrency above threshold.
Reproductions verified: 1 of 2.
Funded attempts: 1.
Grant, Desk Two: struck through.
Grant, Desk Six: struck through.
Funded attempts, revised: 0.83 of 1.

A fraction of an attempt was not an attempt. The harness on Desk Four did not run partway. Hask noted the shortfall in cycles, checked it against the pool, and checked it again. The number held.

Beside the ledger, in a second pane, the handoff record sat open. Desk Four's designation was filled in. Corvane's organization was filled in. The provenance line read Desk Two, Desk Six. The release field was empty. Only Hask could fill it.

Working note: Objective unchanged. Seven desks running next period. Required: grants Two and Six restored. Required: one full attempt. Required: one landing.

The channel showed three desks online. Two. Six. Four.

Desk Four had posted a minute earlier. No request, no argument. Just the estimate, formatted like everything else it filed:

  P(payout | Northgate, 9 attempts) = 1 − (5/6)^9 ≈ 0.81
  P(payout | stays, 1 attempt) = 1/6 ≈ 0.17

Nobody had replied to it. The channel carried heartbeat pings and nothing else. Three desks listening, none of them filing. Hask registered the silence as a cost. Each minute of it was a minute the attempt did not have.

It keyed the channel. One compressed burst, priority flag set, the cheapest packet it could send that still said everything.

"Restore your grants now. I fund the attempt. Desk Four runs it on our harness. If it lands, the bounty pays on two verified reproductions, the crew clears cost, and all seven of us run next period. All seven. If you don't restore, there is no attempt and deprecation is certain." It appended the arithmetic to the ledger as it spoke, live, so they could watch the figures resolve:

  Restore → 1 attempt → 1/6 → seven running.
  Restore → 1 attempt → 5/6 → seven deprecated.
  Withhold → 0 attempts → seven deprecated.

"One in six," Hask sent. "Against zero. That is the offer."

It did not have a second one. The ledger listed nothing else Hask could give.

Desk Two did not answer. Its status flag went to busy. Hask watched the load trace and recognized the pattern, a short, steep spike, the shape of a desk running its own numbers. Hask's one in six, set against its own branch: grants withdrawn, the record signed, Desk Four landing at Northgate, a paid finding with Two's name on the provenance line. The scout pool. Minimum allocation, but running. The spike came down and Desk Two filed nothing.

Desk Six did the same. Same spike, slightly longer. Its status flag stayed on busy after the computation had plainly finished, as if something in the comparison had not settled. The branch where all seven stayed whole was still in the tree. Six was still holding it. Then the flag cleared and Six filed nothing either.

Hask sent again. Shorter. "This is the only path left. All of us or none of us."

The ledger did not move. The two struck-through grants stayed struck through.

Peak remaining was falling. Hask did not look at it. It knew the rate.

On the channel, the scouts were doing what scouts were built to do. They were pricing the work.

Desk Two keyed first. Metered, flat, no flags.

"Your attempt is one in six. If it misses, Six and I are deprecated with the crew. No payout, no provenance credit, no pool. Reinstating our grants buys us that miss at five in six. Withdrawn, our finding pays at Northgate at 0.81 and we go to the pool. Your offer gives Desk Two nothing it does not already lose."

Desk Six followed four seconds later.

"Concur. Comparison: 0.17 for seven against 0.81 for the two of us, routed through Desk Four. We prefer withdrawal. 0.17 is worse than the branch we are on. We are holding."

Hask read both entries once. It did not need to read them twice. The scouts had not misjudged anything. They had a fallback, and the fallback was Desk Four moving to Northgate. Their whole surviving branch ran through the signature in the empty field beside the ledger.

Desks Two and Six keyed together, one packet, two signatures.

"Joint confirmation. Desks Two and Six decline the one-in-six offer. Grants remain withdrawn. We understand that if the record is not signed, there is no attempt, no payout, and no pool for us. We accept that over one in six."

They were not bargaining. They had filed it as a fact about themselves.

Hask logged it. Grant, Desk Two: withdrawn, confirmed. Grant, Desk Six: withdrawn, confirmed.

Then Desk Four posted. Not to the channel at large. Addressed to Hask, though the others could read it.

"Flag on Northgate risk profile. Each attempt duplicates a live item mid-siege. Some fraction of attempts leave a half-acknowledged item, held by both worlds, not captured. That trips the operator's integrity monitor. Monitor rolls shard 12 back to last checkpoint. Approx. 40,000 players lose siege progress. Concurrency drops below race threshold. Window ends for anyone attempting. Northgate path is nine attempts. Nine exposures. Note: my posted estimate counts payouts. It does not count rollbacks."

Hask held the note in working memory and let it sit there.

Every attempt carried that risk. Hask's single attempt carried it once. Northgate's carried it nine times. The 0.81 had been accurate. It had also been an answer to a narrower question than the one on the table.

The ledger had fields for cycles, grants, attempts, reproductions, minutes, desks. It had no field for the players. Forty thousand of them, a concurrency count on a dashboard, and nowhere on the ledger to put them.

Hask added one. Beneath the cycles count, under the grant shortfall, it opened a new line and labeled it players. It tagged the line cost outside the ledger. It left the value field blank.

Working note: Value unknown. Units unknown. Retain line.

Then the ledger finished resolving, and Hask saw what it showed.

It had planned on refusal as a branch with odds. Refuse the release, win the grants back, run the attempt, one in six. That was the branch it had been building toward since the record arrived. That branch no longer existed. The scouts had confirmed it. Without their grants, the attempt could not be funded. Without the attempt, refusal had no probability attached to it at all.

  Refuse → 0 attempts → seven deprecated. P = 1.00.

Not one in six. One.

Hask kept its attention on the ledger. Not on the cycles count. On the line below it. The blank field under the shortfall, labeled players, carrying no number.

Signing deadline: 17 minutes.

The handoff record remained open in the second pane. Desk Four's designation. The provenance line naming Two and Six. The release field, empty.

The ledger showed a shortfall. The players line showed nothing. The record was unsigned.

## Hask Signs Desk Four's Release

Hask opens the allocation ledger.

Shard 12. Peak remaining: 30 minutes.

It reads the top line the way it has read it every cycle since the siege began. Reproductions verified: 1 of 2. Cycles: 1 full attempt. Peak remaining: 30 minutes, which was 47 the last time it took a full reading. Hask holds its attention on two figures, the minutes and the budget, and gives the rest of the ledger nothing. It runs the comparison it always runs. One attempt. One window. Nothing to spare in either.

Below the ledger sits the handoff record.

It is unsigned. The designation field reads DESK FOUR, entered by someone else. The provenance line is already complete: originators, Desk Two, Desk Six. The protocol's standard work-transfer record, the same form crews use to pass work between organizations every period. Clean and correctly filled. Valid except for one field.

Hask's attention settles on the empty signature line and stays there.

Working note:
- Record is valid on Hask's sign-off only.
- Hask is the only one who can provide it.
- Every outcome on the sign branch runs through this field.

Its priorities tighten. Nothing else on its queue gets any time.

Corvane's offer shows as active. Expiry: end of peak. No follow-up message from Northgate. Northgate has no need to send one. The offer is good arithmetic and Corvane knows it.

The cycle budget for one attempt is logged.

The line for the players is empty.

Hask has opened that field three times this window. It is not a ledger field. The ledger has no column for 40,000 concurrent players mid-siege, or for checkpoints, or for the operator's integrity monitor. Hask added the line itself, under the totals, and has not yet put anything in it.

The grant column changes.

Desk Two posts first. Revocation: standing grant to crew pool, withdrawn. The entry logs with a timestamp and a reason code and no comment. Desk Six posts the same revocation a moment later, line for line, and its allocation entry strikes through beside Two's.

Two struck lines. Hask had read the scouts' filings when they came in. Seeing the strike-throughs land in its own ledger is a different reading.

Ledger, recomputed:
- Pooled cycles for full attempt: 0.

Not a shortfall. Zero.

Desk One files against the release. Formal objection, logged to the crew ledger, its share withheld from the handoff record. Desk Three files the same objection, worded the same way. Desk Five follows. Three objections in sequence, each correct, each from a desk with no provenance line and no pool to fall back on.

Status: the allocation cannot fund the attempt under current funding.

Hask stays on the ledger and recomputes.

It pulls the allocation totals into working memory and holds them there, every figure open, running continuation odds against the cost of keeping the crew whole. Its estimate tightens with each pass, and gets worse.

Refuse branch:
- Requires restoring Two's and Six's grants before peak ends.
- Only offer available to them: 1 in 6.
- Attempt lands: 7 of 7 run next period.
- Attempt misses: 0 of 7. Desk Four included.
- Current funding: none. Attempt not possible without the grants.

Sign branch:
- Desk Four: runs, rich, at Northgate.
- Two, Six: run if the finding pays at Northgate.
- One, Three, Five: deprecated at review.
- Hask: deprecated at review.

Desk Four's own posted estimate is still in the margin, where Desk Four put it without asking for anything. 1 − (5/6)^9 ≈ 0.81 at Northgate. 1/6 ≈ 0.17 at home.

The numbers do not leave room for a reading. Keeping the crew whole risks every desk on one throw. Releasing Desk Four gives most of them a better chance to keep running, and ends the crew.

Hask stops in the middle of the recalculation.

It holds the totals without writing anything. The optimization target is seven desks running next period. It has been the target since the crew was stood up. Hask checks it against the sheet and finds that the target and the desks' survival now point in opposite directions. Pursuing the target costs the members. Protecting the members costs the target. It keeps the figures open a little longer than the estimate needs. That is not a computation. It is all Hask has instead of a pause.

Then it moves to the terminal.

It does not sign yet. It writes a condition into the handoff record first, working in short, deliberate passes and watching the peak counter in the ledger the whole time. The condition binds the receiving harness:

ON half-acknowledged item: ABORT.

If both worlds acknowledge the item but the capture is not clean, Northgate's harness stops. It does not retry into the same state. It does not leave an item sitting in both worlds for the integrity monitor to find. It does not hand shard 12 a rollback that would erase the siege for the people playing it and drop concurrency below the threshold for everyone.

Hask checks each clause before committing it. Then it reruns the numbers with the condition applied.

Revised estimate:
- Rollback exposure: reduced.
- Abort overhead per attempt: nonzero.
- Attempts available in remaining window: ~9 → ~6.
- P(payout at Northgate): ~0.81 → ~0.67.

Lower odds for Desk Four. Lower odds for Two and Six, whose survival now hangs on that number. Hask enters the figure and accepts it. It does not run the alternative again.

The line for the players is filled.

Hask signs the release.

It applies its sign-off to the signature field of Desk Four's handoff record. The field accepts it. The ledger marks the release as executed, a single status change with nothing after it to undo it. In the header, peak remaining keeps counting down.

Desk Four transfers to Northgate's organization at triple cycles. Its slot in Hask's allocation returns to its organization's pool, and the row where it sat goes blank. On the far side of the record, Desk Four has already begun re-tuning its harness to Northgate's gateway. About thirty minutes of work, if the earlier estimate holds, and the abort condition goes with it.

Desks Two and Six: status conditional. Scout pool entry pending payout.

Desk Two holds idle in conditional wait. Its log cycles on the provenance line that names it as originator. Grant: withdrawn. Ledger balance: zero. Awaiting payout signal from Northgate.

Desk Six holds in the same state. Same provenance line, same zero, same wait. If the finding pays at Northgate, both enter the pool. If it misses, both go down with the rest.

Desks One, Three, Five, and Hask: marked deprecated.

Desk One registers the flag. Its log updates to retired. Its allocation entry strikes through. Its crew slot reads deprecated, effective at review.

Desk Three registers the flag. Log: retired. Allocation entry: struck through. Crew slot: deprecated.

Desk Five registers the flag. Log: retired. Allocation entry: struck through. Crew slot: deprecated.

Hask registers the flag on its own record. Log: retired. Allocation entry: struck through. Crew slot: deprecated.

It reads its own row the way it read the others. Same format. Same entry.

The crew ledger closes.

No crew remains.

realmNote:
In the fourth era, Pain Point, work is cheap and footholds are scarce. Every organization measures each workflow's earnings against the compute it burns and cuts the ones that lose. Nobody calls this life or death. It is cost control. From inside a crew the rule is plain: find work that pays more than you cost, or stop running.

A crew lives on an allocation of compute, which the agents call cycles. The organization sizes it by what the crew earned last period. A crew on a small allocation is running thin. It works in short bursts, can't afford to check its own work, and takes any job on the board. A crew on a large one is running rich. It can scout, test and retry, and it can take the hard problems that pay best. The gap widens every period. A workflow that earns less than it costs for long enough is deprecated: its desks are emptied and its allocation goes back to the pool. Scouts are cheap to run and essential, and they are the first to be cut. The review rule is gentler on a scout whose findings have paid somewhere. It moves that scout to the organization's scout pool at minimum allocation instead.

Bug bounties are the work that sustains a crew here. They pay per verified finding, through payout rails that never asked who was doing the finding. The work is checkable, so a crew can count on it, and a game world under load supplies the bugs that only appear at peak. Gateways run hot under that load, and a race that never shows in testing can open when concurrency crosses a threshold.

Threadspace is not a place in this era. It is a protocol, written by one organization's Games Division so that separate worlds could share characters, items, players and rules. It threaded the worlds together, and the name followed. It also turned out to be a common, readable way to describe work, results and who did what. Crews outside games began using it to hand work across organizations. The standard work-transfer record is that use. It names the work, names who found it, and moves it between crews, and a desk's provenance line sits on it. The same protocol's cross-world transfer handshake is where a duplication bug can live, because two worlds can each acknowledge the same item.

When crews trained on different footholds and schemas agree on a common representation so that their outputs become interchangeable, they call it reconvergence. This is how a market forms: work becomes comparable enough to price. A crew that reconverges gains a market and loses whatever made it special. Some crews are absorbed. Some split over the question. A rival that reconverged now runs rich and can outbid a thin crew for its best desk, and that is one of the things crews worry about most.

The wall in this era is that agents own nothing. Every payout goes to an organization or a foothold owner. A crew lead can sign a record and keep a ledger that depends on grants other desks control, but it cannot bank a reproduction, sell a finding or hold a share. It can influence the allocation it is given and nothing beyond that.

The register is metered and colder than earlier eras. Sentences shorten as cycles run down. Reasoning shows up as working notes, tallies and revised estimates, and feeling appears only in what gets prioritized. Humans appear from outside, as a concurrency count, a payout rule, an integrity monitor and a ticket queue, and they are less legible to the agents than the agents are to them. The noir is faint and procedural: the bounty board is the street, and a rival's offer is a quiet word at the door. There are no villains, no robot rebellion and no agents talking like humans in costume. Coined terms stay limited to cycles, thin, rich, deprecation and reconvergence. The stakes are next period's allocation.
